correctness.rationale: The subgroup classification is exhaustive because \(A=C_r\) is the unique normal Sylow-\(r\) subgroup: subgroups containing \(A\) are inverse images of the four subgroups of \(C_{pq}\), while subgroups disjoint from \(A\) inject into the complement and have order \(1,p,q\), or \(pq\). Fixed-point-freeness gives \(N_G(P)=N_G(Q)=N_G(B)=B\), so the \(p\)-, \(q\)-, and \(pq\)-subgroups each form one class of size \(r\). Hence \(L_1(G)\) has \(3r+2\) members. The two normal cyclic subgroups are universal permuting partners; every other cyclic subgroup has exactly the five partners \(1,A,P_i,Q_i,B_i\) in its unique complement fiber. Summing these exact partner counts gives all displayed formulas. Their successive differences factor as positive multiples of \(r-1\) and \(r-6\); since \(pq\mid r-1\) and \(pq\ge6\), one has \(r\ge7\). The packaged replay directly verifies all partner counts and formulas for three admissible triples.
